Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Institution: Radboudumc | Date: 10 Feb 2025

Clinical query initiated for a 66-year-old gentleman exhibiting a PSA trajectory culminating at 12.0 following a previous biopsy event.

FINDINGS: Prostatic dimensions total 69.24 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a sharply demarcated, intensely hypointense focus within the right mid-to-apical peripheral compartment, spanning roughly 18 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging exhibits pronounced restriction, mirrored by suppressed ADC signals across b-values 0, 1000, and 2000 s/mm². Post-contrast phases capture early, focal, and robust enhancement localized to the focus. Extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle invasion are absent. Pelvic lymph nodes maintain normal size and architecture.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 focus situated in the right mid-apical peripheral zone. Prostate-specific antigen density registers 0.173 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.8477834.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: January 2024 marked the initial PSA elevation at 4.7 ng/mL, triggering specialist assessment. A follow-up measurement in May climbed to 5.8 ng/mL, which drove the decision to order a multiparametric MRI alongside targeted biopsy planning. During the intervening months, serial PSA tracking and symptom monitoring continued regularly. The latest January 2025 draw recorded 12.0 ng/mL, initiating this current outpatient urological consultation.
